extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). Tasks cover single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, with 4,750 test instances total.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation Chinese Academy of Sciences
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from multiple sources including existing datasets (NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader) and manually curated datasets (MultiFieldQA). For MultiFieldQA, documents were collected from legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers, etc., and three Ph.D. students annotated question-answer pairs. Multi-document QA contexts were constructed by combining supporting and distracting Wikipedia passages until reaching a maximum length.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data includes: NarrativeQA (literature and film stories), Qasper (NLP papers), MultiFieldQA (legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers), HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue (Wikipedia-based), and DuReader (Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao, comprising 200K questions and 1M related documents).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three Ph.D. students annotated questions and answers for each article in MultiFieldQA datasets, ensuring answers can be inferred from documents and evidence placement is random to avoid positional biases.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotators per item for MultiFieldQA datasets
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was constructed with care to avoid placement biases in evidence location, ensuring answer-related statements are not consistently found at the beginning or end of documents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses automated evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) which may not fully capture model performance. Some models still experience significant performance decline as context length increases despite being trained on longer contexts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: LongBench is designed for evaluating (testing) large language models' long context understanding capabilities across multiple tasks including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, in both English and Chinese.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two extraction strategies were used: random sampling to maintain natural length distribution, and uniform sampling based on data length to study model capabilities across varying context lengths. For multi-doc QA, supporting passages were included first, then distracting passages were added until maximum length was reached, and passages were randomly ordered. For DuReader, several documents related to the question plus arbitrarily selected distractors were included until each question had 20 documents.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage (except VCSUM). For multi-doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs were used as context. For MultiFieldQA, Ph.D. students annotated question-answer pairs ensuring answers can be inferred from documents and evidence placement was randomized to avoid positional biases.
